subtopics.title: Section planes and what is drawn
subtopics.theory_md:
A **section plane** (cutting plane) cuts the solid and the part between it and the observer is removed; the cut face is **hatched**: thin lines at $45^\circ$, 2 to 3 mm apart.

Four useful positions:
- **Perpendicular to VP, inclined to HP** (an AIP-type plane): a line in the FV (its VT); the TV section is foreshortened.
- **Perpendicular to HP, inclined to VP** (AVP): a line in the TV (its HT).
- **Parallel to HP**: section is its true shape in the TV. **Parallel to VP**: true shape in the FV.

A plane inclined to the view appears as a line only in the view it is perpendicular to. Its **true shape** needs an auxiliary view with $x_1y_1$ parallel to that line.
subtopics.basics_md: Slice a loaf of bread. The cut face is the section. If you look straight at the cut face you see its real size; if you look from the side it looks squashed. That squashed picture is the apparent section; the straight-on picture is the true shape.
key_points: Section plane cuts the solid; the part towards the observer is removed
Cut face hatched with thin lines at 45 degrees
Plane perpendicular to VP: line in FV (VT); perpendicular to HP: line in TV (HT)
Plane parallel to HP/VP gives the true shape directly in TV/FV
Otherwise the true shape is found by an auxiliary view with x1y1 parallel to the section line

questions.q: State the four common positions of a section plane and say in which view each appears as a line.
questions.model_answer_md:
1. **Perpendicular to VP, inclined to HP:** a line in the FV (VT); TV section is apparent, true shape needs an auxiliary view.
2. **Perpendicular to HP, inclined to VP:** a line in the TV (HT).
3. **Parallel to HP:** a line in the FV; true shape in the TV.
4. **Parallel to VP:** a line in the TV; true shape in the FV.

subtopics.title: Pyramid cut by a plane perpendicular to VP and inclined to HP
subtopics.theory_md:
Standard job: pyramid on its base on the HP, section plane perpendicular to the VP at $\theta$ to the HP, through a stated point of the axis.

1. Draw TV and FV of the pyramid.
2. Draw the **section line** in the FV through the point at $\theta$ to XY; mark $1',2',3'\dots$ where it crosses the slant edges.
3. Project each point **down onto the same edge** in the TV; join in order: the **sectional TV**, hatched.
4. **True shape:** $x_1y_1$ parallel to the section line, projectors perpendicular to it, distances taken from XY in the TV; join.

The cut part (above the line) is removed in the FV. If the line leaves through the base, the base edge is cut too.
subtopics.basics_md: Think of a tent cut by a knife. In the front view the knife is a straight line. Where it crosses each rope-edge of the tent gives one corner of the cut face. Drop those corners straight down to the plan, onto the same ropes.
key_points: Section line in FV through the given axis point at the given angle to XY
Cut points on slant edges projected to the same edges in TV
Sectional TV joined in order and hatched at 45 degrees
True shape on x1y1 parallel to section line, distances from XY of the TV
Cut part removed in FV; final answer shows FV, sectional TV and true shape

questions.model_answer_md:
**Setup.** Half-diagonal of base $=30/\sqrt2=21.21$ mm. The extreme edges in the FV run from the apex (60 mm) to the corners at $\pm21.21$ mm. Plane through the axis midpoint (30 mm height), slope $\tan40^\circ$.

**Right edge:** $z=60(1-x/21.21)$ and $z=30-x\tan40^\circ$ gives $x=15.08$ mm, $z=17.35$ mm.
**Left edge:** $z=60(1-x/21.21)$ and $z=30+x\tan40^\circ$ gives $x=8.18$ mm (left), $z=36.86$ mm.

**Length along the cut line** $=\sqrt{(15.08+8.18)^2+(36.86-17.35)^2}=30.36$ mm.

The other two edges are cut at 30 mm height on the axis line, 10.61 mm to either side of the FV axis in the TV, so the true shape is a four-sided figure with diagonals 30.36 mm and 21.21 mm.

subtopics.title: Plane perpendicular to HP, or parallel to a reference plane
subtopics.theory_md:
**Plane perpendicular to HP, inclined to VP (AVP):** the section line is drawn in the **TV** through the stated point at $\phi$ to XY (its HT). Cut points are projected **up** to the same edges in the FV to give the **sectional FV**. True shape: $x_1y_1$ parallel to the TV section line, projectors perpendicular to it, and distance of each point from $x_1y_1$ equals its **height above XY** in the FV.

**Plane parallel to VP** (a distance from the axis): the TV shows a line parallel to XY; the section is its **true shape in the FV**, so no auxiliary view is needed. Remove the part nearer the observer.
subtopics.basics_md: Same method as before, with the views swapped. The plane is edge-on in the plan this time, so you mark cuts in the plan and lift them to the elevation. Heights come from the elevation.
key_points: AVP section line is drawn in the TV at the given angle to XY
Cut points projected up to the same edges in the FV give the sectional FV
True shape on x1y1 parallel to the TV line; distances are heights from the FV
Plane parallel to VP: section is true shape in the FV; no auxiliary view
Part nearer the observer is removed; hatch at 45 degrees

subtopics.title: Cone cut by a plane perpendicular to VP: ellipse, parabola, hyperbola
subtopics.theory_md:
For a cone cut by a plane perpendicular to the VP, compare the plane's angle $\theta$ to the base with the generator angle $\alpha=\tan^{-1}(h/r)$:
- through the apex: **triangle**
- parallel to the base: **circle**
- $\theta<\alpha$ (cuts all generators): **ellipse**
- $\theta=\alpha$ (parallel to one generator): **parabola**
- $\theta>\alpha$, or parallel to the axis: **hyperbola**

For the curve: divide the base circle into 12 generators, mark where the section line cuts each in the FV, project to the TV on the same generators, join with a smooth curve. For the ellipse, the **major axis** is the cut line in the FV; the minor axis is the chord at the midpoint of the major axis, not at the axis point.
subtopics.basics_md: A cone cut like a carrot: cut straight across gives a circle; slanted but all the way through gives an oval; cut parallel to the side gives a one-ended parabola; cut steep gives a hyperbola.
key_points: Conic types decided by comparing the plane angle with the generator angle alpha
Ellipse when the plane angle is less than alpha; parabola when equal; hyperbola when greater
Generators drawn in FV and TV, cut points projected to the same generators
Major axis is the cut line in the FV
Smooth curve through the points; hatch the section

questions.why: $\theta=45^\circ<67.4^\circ$, so the plane cuts every generator: ellipse.

questions.q: A cone of base diameter 50 mm and axis 60 mm stands on its base on the HP. A plane perpendicular to the VP and inclined at $45^\circ$ to the HP passes through the midpoint of the axis. Find the major and minor axes of the section.
questions.model_answer_md:
**Generator angle:** $\tan^{-1}(60/25)=67.4^\circ>45^\circ$, so the section is an **ellipse**.

**Cut points in the FV** (plane $z=30-x\tan45^\circ$, generators $z=60(1-|x|/25)$):
- right generator: $x=21.43$ mm, $z=8.57$ mm
- left generator: $x=8.82$ mm (left), $z=38.82$ mm

**Major axis** $=\sqrt{(21.43+8.82)^2+(38.82-8.57)^2}=42.78$ mm (the cut line in the FV).

**Minor axis:** midpoint of the major axis at $x=6.30$ mm, $z=23.70$ mm; cone radius there $=25(1-23.70/60)=15.13$ mm; minor axis $=2\sqrt{15.13^2-6.30^2}=27.5$ mm.

Generator cut points: (21.43, 8.57) and (8.82 left, 38.82)
Major axis 42.78 mm
Minor axis 27.5 mm, at the midpoint of the major axis
Units in mm

questions.q: A cone of base diameter 50 mm and axis 60 mm is cut by a plane perpendicular to the VP and parallel to a generator, through the point on the axis 30 mm above the base. Name the curve and find its vertex and the axis length of the curve.
questions.model_answer_md:
Generator angle $67.4^\circ$, so the plane is at $67.4^\circ$ to the HP: a **parabola**.

Plane: $z=30+x_l\tan67.4^\circ$ on the left, generator $z=60-2.4x_l$. So $4.8x_l=30$, $x_l=6.25$ mm, vertex $z=45$ mm.

On the right the plane meets the base at $x=12.5$ mm. Length of the curve's axis (vertex to base) $=\sqrt{(6.25+12.5)^2+45^2}=48.75$ mm.

subtopics.title: Auxiliary inclined plane (AIP) as the cutting plane
subtopics.theory_md:
An **AIP** is a plane perpendicular to the VP and inclined to the HP. In the FV it is a line; the TV of the section is foreshortened. An **AVP** (auxiliary vertical plane) is perpendicular to the HP and inclined to the VP; it is a line in the TV.

Steps for a pyramid in simple position: FV/TV; section line in the FV through the stated point (e.g. midpoint of axis) at $\theta$ to XY; cut points on the slant edges; project to the TV on the same edges; **sectional TV**; the FV of the remaining solid is the **sectional FV** (cut line as the top edge). For a hexagonal pyramid, a plane at $30^\circ$ through the midpoint of a 70 mm axis cuts all six slant edges.
subtopics.basics_md: The AIP is the 'knife seen edge-on in the elevation'. You draw it as a straight inclined line in the front view, and everything else follows from where that line crosses the edges.
key_points: AIP: perpendicular to VP, inclined to HP; a line in the FV
AVP: perpendicular to HP, inclined to VP; a line in the TV
Section line through the stated axis point at the stated angle to XY
Cut points projected to the same edges in the other view
Sectional TV hatched; remaining solid shown in FV with the cut line

subtopics.title: True shape of the section: the auxiliary view
subtopics.theory_md:
The section is at its **true shape** when viewed perpendicular to the cutting plane. So:
1. Draw $x_1y_1$ **parallel** to the section line, a convenient distance away.
2. Draw projectors from each cut point **perpendicular** to the section line.
3. On each projector measure from $x_1y_1$ the distance the point has from **XY in the other view** (TV for an AIP, FV heights for an AVP).
4. Join in the same order; hatch at $45^\circ$.

True length of the section along the cut line is the length of the line itself, since it is parallel to $x_1y_1$. Every point keeps its order, so a quadrilateral section gives a quadrilateral.
subtopics.basics_md: To see the real shape of the cut face you walk round until you look at it face-on. Drawing-wise that means drawing a new ground line parallel to the edge-on line, and putting each point at its old distance from the old ground line.
key_points: x1y1 parallel to the section line
Projectors perpendicular to the section line
Distance from x1y1 equals distance from XY in the other view
Join in order and hatch at 45 degrees
Length along the cut line in the true shape equals the cut line length

questions.q: A square pyramid (base 40 mm, axis 60 mm, sides equally inclined to the VP) is cut by a plane perpendicular to the VP, at $45^\circ$ to the HP, bisecting the axis. Give the dimensions of the true shape.
questions.model_answer_md:
Section points (x from axis, y from axis in the TV, z height): $(26.75, 0, 3.25)$, $(0, 14.14, 30)$, $(-9.61, 0, 39.61)$, $(0, -14.14, 30)$ mm.

On $x_1y_1$ parallel to the cut line, the distances along the line are $16.62$, $-21.21$, $-34.81$, $-21.21$ mm and widths $0, \pm14.14, 0$ mm.

So the true shape is a **kite**, length $16.62+34.81=51.43$ mm along the cut line and width $2\times14.14=28.28$ mm at 21.21 mm from the lower end.
points: True shape is a kite
Length 51.43 mm along the cut line
Width 28.28 mm

subtopics.title: Solid in a tilted position, then cut
subtopics.theory_md:
For a solid resting on a face or edge, or with its axis inclined, draw it **in two stages**: first with the base on the HP (simple position), then tilt the FV by the required angle about the corner or edge in contact and project the TV (keeping the axis parallel to the VP if so stated). Then add the cutting plane in the view where it appears as a line: an AVP in the TV (HT at the given angle to XY), and find the sectional FV from it.

Pentagonal pyramid (side 30, axis 60) on a triangular face: apothem of base $=15/\tan36^\circ=20.65$ mm, face makes $\tan^{-1}(60/20.65)=71.0^\circ$ with the base, so the axis is inclined $19.0^\circ$ to the HP.
subtopics.basics_md: First stand the solid up normally. Then tip it until it rests on the face you want. Only after that do you draw the knife. The cuts are always found in the tipped drawing.
key_points: Draw the solid in simple position first, then tilt for the final position

Cutting plane (AVP) is a line in the TV at the given angle
Cut points projected up to the FV give the sectional FV
True shape on x1y1 parallel to the TV line, heights from the FV

subtopics.title: Frustum and truncated solid
subtopics.theory_md:
A **frustum** is what remains of a cone or pyramid when the top is cut off by a plane **parallel to the base**; its FV is a trapezium and its TV is two concentric figures. A **truncated solid** is cut by a plane **inclined** to the base and the part above is removed; it has no top face of the same shape.

The frustum's full cone/pyramid is found by similar triangles: apex height $H=h\,r_1/(r_1-r_2)$, where $h$ is the frustum height, $r_1$ the base and $r_2$ the top radius. For a base of 50 mm diameter, top 25 mm and height 50 mm: $H=50\times25/12.5=100$ mm. A section parallel to the base at $z$ above it has radius $r_1(1-z/H)$.
subtopics.basics_md: Cut the top off an ice-cream cone with a straight horizontal cut: the bit left is a frustum. Cut slantwise: it is a truncated cone.
key_points: Frustum: cone or pyramid with the top cut by a plane parallel to the base
Truncated solid: cut by an inclined plane, upper part removed
Apex height of the full solid H = h r1/(r1 - r2) by similar triangles
Parallel section is a similar figure; radius r1(1 - z/H)

subtopics.title: Section of a frustum by an inclined plane
subtopics.theory_md:
For a **cone frustum** cut by a plane perpendicular to the VP at $\theta$ to the HP, extend the generators to the full cone, find the cut with the generators, and check each point lies between the base and the top face. If the line meets the **top face**, the curve stops there and a straight (chord) edge closes the section; if it meets the base, the cut leaves through the base circle.

The method: 12 generators, section line in the FV, project each cut point to the TV on its generator, join with a smooth curve, then the true shape on $x_1y_1$ parallel to the cut line.

For base $\varnothing50$, top $\varnothing25$, height 50, a plane at $45^\circ$ through the 30 mm level meets the generators at 6.67 mm and 44 mm height, both inside the frustum.
subtopics.basics_md: Imagine the frustum is still part of a bigger cone. Cut it the same way as the cone, but throw away the points that would be outside the real solid.
key_points: Extend the frustum to the full cone for the generators
Section line in the FV at the given angle through the given point
Cut points must lie between base and top; otherwise the section is cut by the top face or base
Project to the TV on the same generators; smooth curve
True shape on x1y1 parallel to the cut line; ellipse axes from the cut line

questions.q: A frustum has base $\varnothing50$ mm, top $\varnothing25$ mm and height 50 mm. A plane perpendicular to the VP and inclined at $45^\circ$ to the HP passes through the point 30 mm up the axis. Find the major and minor axes of the section.
questions.model_answer_md:
Full cone: $H=100$ mm, base radius 25 mm.

**Cut points:** right generator $x=23.33$ mm, $z=6.67$ mm; left generator $x=14.00$ mm (left), $z=44.00$ mm. Both are between 0 and 50 mm so the whole ellipse lies on the slant surface.

**Major axis** $=\sqrt{(23.33+14.00)^2+(44.00-6.67)^2}=52.80$ mm.

**Minor axis** at the midpoint: $x=4.67$ mm, $z=25.33$ mm; radius there $=25(1-25.33/100)=18.67$ mm; minor $=2\sqrt{18.67^2-4.67^2}=36.15$ mm.
points: Full cone 100 mm high, radius 25 mm
Both within the frustum, so complete ellipse
Major axis 52.80 mm
Minor axis 36.15 mm

subtopics.title: Views of the remaining (truncated) solid
subtopics.theory_md:
After the section, **draw the remaining solid** in both views.
- Sectional view of the cut: hatched at $45^\circ$ (the cut face).
- The view in which the plane is a line (FV for a plane perpendicular to the VP) shows the remaining outline with the **cut line as the top edge**; no hatching.
- In the other view, the outline of the solid is unchanged where it is below the cut; the cut part's edges are not drawn.
- Edges between the cut points and the retained corners are shown as **thick** lines, the removed edges are erased (or thin).

Label the cut points $1,2,3\dots$; state the shape of the section and its true shape.
subtopics.basics_md: After you cut, tidy the drawing: show only what is left, with the cut face shaded. Everything above the knife disappears.

questions.q: State, with reasons, what is shown in the FV and TV after a pyramid is cut by a plane perpendicular to the VP.
questions.model_answer_md:
**FV:** the retained part is the pyramid below the section line; the cut face is edge-on, so a straight line with **no hatching**.

**TV:** the retained edges up to the cut points, and the closed section figure **hatched at $45^\circ$** (the apparent section).

**Auxiliary view:** the true shape, drawn on $x_1y_1$ parallel to the section line, also hatched.

Base outline remains in both views.
points: FV shows the cut face as a line, no hatching
TV shows the apparent section hatched at 45 degrees
True shape in an auxiliary view
Removed part is not drawn
